'''Shoumogu''' (聖母宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Iki, Nagasaki|en|Iki, Nagasaki|qid=Q861519|lt=Iki City}}, Nagasaki Prefecture, in Katsumoto Town. Listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, it is considered a potential site of the Shikinaisha “Nakatsu Shrine.” However, another shrine currently bearing that name exists separately ({{ill|Nakatsu Shrine (Iki)|ja|中津神社 (壱岐市)}}).

== Enshrined Deities ==
The shrine honors the following deities:
* {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|息長足姫尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okinaga-Tarashihime no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 神功皇后|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q232803}} (Empress Jingū)
* {{ill|Emperor Chūai|ja|足仲彦尊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tarashinakatsuhiko no Mikoto|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 仲哀天皇|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q179971}} (Emperor Chūai)
* {{ill|Uwatsutsunoo no Mikoto|ja|上筒男尊}}, {{ill|Nakatsutsunoo no Mikoto|ja|仲筒男尊}}, and {{ill|Sokotsutsunoo no Mikoto|ja|底筒男尊}} (collectively known as {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|ja|住吉大神|lt=Sumiyoshi Sanjin}})

The shrine is associated with Empress Jingū’s {{ill|Three Han Campaign|ja|三韓征伐|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sankan Seibatsu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11249435}} (conquest of the Three Han States). Known as a deity of victory due to her triumph, she is also venerated as a deity of safe childbirth, as she gave birth to Emperor Ōjin after her victorious return.

== History ==
In the 9th year of Emperor Chūai’s reign (possibly 200 CE), Empress Jingū constructed a temporary palace ({{ill|kinzai|ca|Cort itinerant|da|Rejsekongedømme|de|Reisekönigtum|es|Corte itinerante|fr|Cour itinérante|it|Corte itinerante|ja|行宮|ko|행궁|nl|Ambulant koningschap|no|Reisekongedømme|pt|Corte itinerante|ru|Кочующий королевский двор|sv|Reisekönigtum|uk|Мандрівний суд|zh|行宫|qid=Q2141881}}) in Iki while awaiting favorable winds for her campaign. The area was named “Kazamoto” (Wind Origin) after the northward winds blew. Upon her victorious return in December of the same year, the area was renamed “Katsumoto” (Victory Origin). According to legend, 101,500 enemy heads were buried here.

The palace fell into disuse until a miraculous event involving glowing objects from the sea led to the offering of mirrors and the enshrinement of Empress Jingū. In 717 CE (Yōrō 1), the shrine was formally established, and structures were built to pray for national protection. Over time, it gained prominence as one of Iki’s Seven Great Shrines and the second shrine of Iki Province. It also maintained strong connections to {{ill|Kashii-gū|abstract|Q631373|de|Kashii-gū|fr|Kashii-gū|ja|香椎宮|zh|香椎宮|qid=Q631373|lt=Kashii Shrine}} in Fukuoka.

Despite historical disputes regarding its status as a Shikinaisha, many researchers and reports, such as the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}, suggest that Shoumogu is the original Nakatsu Shrine, while the current Nakatsu Shrine represents a later branch.

The shrine’s name “Seibo” (Holy Mother) and its location in Nagasaki Prefecture often lead to misconceptions about connections with Christianity, but it is entirely unrelated.

== Festivals ==
The annual festival spans five days and is Iki’s largest event. It includes the Goshinkō-sen, a boat procession listed as a {{ill|Intangible Folk Cultural Properties Requiring Documentation|ja|選択無形民俗文化財|lt=Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property}}, which predicts harvests and catches for the coming year. On October 14, the final day, events such as the Daikagura (Great Kagura Dance) of Iki and a costume parade are held. The Katsumoto Port Festival on October 15 is often considered part of the shrine’s festivities, extending the celebration to six days.

== Grounds ==
The shrine grounds feature a horseshoe stone believed to bear the hoofprint of Empress Jingū’s horse during the Three Han campaign. It is also historically significant as the landing site of the Mongol invasions during the {{ill|Battle of Bun'ei|azb|بون ای ساواشی|cs|Bitva Bun'ei|de|Schlacht von Bun’ei|es|Batalla de Bun'ei|fa|نبرد بون‌ای|fr|Bataille de Bun'ei|id|Pertempuran Bun'ei|ja|文永の役|mn|Бүн-эйн тулалдаан|ru|Первое монгольское вторжение в Японию|sh|Bitka Bun'eija|qid=Q2237386|lt=Battle of Bun’ei}}.

The main gate was donated by {{ill|Katō Kiyomasa|az|Katö Kiyomasa|ban|Kato Kiyomasa|be|Като Кіёмаса|ca|Katō Kiyomasa|cs|Kijomasa Kató|de|Katō Kiyomasa|el|Κατό Κιγιομάσα|es|Katō Kiyomasa|eu|Katō Kiyomasa|fa|کاتو کیوماسا|fi|Katō Kiyomasa|fr|Katō Kiyomasa|id|Katō Kiyomasa|it|Katō Kiyomasa|ja|加藤清正|kk|Като Киемаса|ko|가토 기요마사|mr|केटो कियोमासा|ms|Katō Kiyomasa|nl|Kato Kiyomasa|ru|Като Киёмаса|sr|Като Кијомаса|th|คาโต คิโยมาซะ|tr|Katō Kiyomasa|uk|Като Кійомаса|vi|Katō Kiyomasa|wuu|加藤清正|zh|加藤清正|zh_classical|加藤清正|zh_yue|加藤清正|qid=Q1069843|lt=Katō Kiyomasa}} during Toyotomi Hideyoshi’s Korean campaigns. The surrounding stone walls were constructed under Katō’s orders as his troops awaited favorable winds, reflecting the shrine’s deep ties to maritime events.
